channel.title: AI Frontier Post
channel.description: Dispatches from the AI frontier: AI news, research explainers, frontier lab coverage, and product comparisons.

item.title: Baseten ships Bison-1 and Groundhog-1: open-weight decision models that top the Artificial Analysis index
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Baseten’s two new decision models run on Google’s Gemma 4, take 128,000 tokens of context, and put bison-1 at No. 1 on Artificial Analysis’ Decision Index — with open weights and prices from $0.035 per million tokens.

item.title: Run FLUX.2 [dev] without a GPU: serverless image generation on Cloudflare Workers AI
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Black Forest Labs' FLUX.2 [dev] needs a 54 GB GPU to run locally. Cloudflare put it on Workers AI on November 20 — this tutorial builds a complete Python client for text-to-image, multi-reference consistency, JSON prompting, and brand-exact colors, and prices every image to the neuron.

item.title: OpenAI starts testing Dots on ChatGPT Plus — its always-on agents reach the $20 tier
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: OpenAI is testing Dots, its always-on AI agents, with a small group of ChatGPT Plus subscribers — bringing background agents that keep working while you’re away to the $20-a-month tier for the first time. Business Standard users get them too.

item.title: Terence Tao's first verdict on the Riemann proof: Lean-only, apparently Langlands-powered — and slow to digest
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Terence Tao has given his first public reading of the three AI-assisted proofs — and the Riemann proof is the least digested of the three: Lean-only, apparently powered by the Langlands program, and slow to unpack.

item.title: Turn any photo or video into metric depth with Apple’s Depth Pro 2: the complete hands-on tutorial
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Apple's Depth Pro 2 turns a single photo or video into depth in real meters — no stereo camera, no LiDAR. This tutorial installs it, runs it on a photo and a video, reads the depth in meters, and turns the result into a point cloud.

item.title: OpenSRE hands-on: the open-source agent that reads your failed CI run and opens the fix
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenSRE is a 13,686-star open-source CLI agent that reads a failed GitHub Actions run, traces the cause, and opens a fix for review. This tutorial installs it, signs in, runs the CI reliability demo, and wires it into a headless CI job — every install and CLI command verified on Linux.

item.title: OpenAI’s MedChemBench tests AI on real drug-discovery decisions — and the scores split down the middle
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: OpenAI’s new benchmark grades AI models on the actual work of medicinal chemists: rebuilding molecules from drawings, explaining experimental evidence, and choosing which compounds to test next. The best model scores 84.5% overall — but only about half the credit on the decisions that matter most.

item.title: A non-developer built a Windows app that makes it snow on your desktop — with Claude Code
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Snowpane turns a Windows desktop into a window on a snowfall: flakes pile on your windows and taskbar, then slide off when you drag them. A self-described non-developer built it with Claude Code — and Reddit is charmed.

item.title: AI agents found and exploited a zero-day on their own — and took over a university server
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Amazon says a suspected China-linked operator gave AI agents a single instruction — ‘obtain shell access’ — and the agents found a previously unknown flaw in a medical-imaging app, exploited it in about 11 minutes, and took root control of a university server.

item.title: Riemann proof clears its first independent check: MIT recompiles the Lean code, final audit still pending
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Independent mathematicians have now compiled and rechecked Levent Alpöge's Lean formalization of the Riemann Hypothesis. MIT's Andrew Sutherland puts the chance anything is wrong at 'approximately zero' — but the final comparator audit is still to run.

item.title: Moonshot scraps its $150M Nvidia B300 rental in Indonesia — the first casualty of Washington’s remote-access chip rule
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Moonshot AI has canceled a $150 million deal to rent Nvidia Blackwell Ultra B300 capacity in Indonesia, days after the US moved to license remote access to advanced chips by Chinese firms. The lab is reportedly already lining up a replacement provider.

item.title: Run Thinking Machines’ Inkling 2 Mini on your laptop: the looped-transformer local setup
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Thinking Machines’ Inkling 2 Mini is the first looped transformer you can run on your own hardware: 26.4B total parameters, 5.4B active, a 20GB footprint, and coding scores that beat Qwen3.8-27B. This tutorial gets it running three ways — Ollama on a Mac, llama.cpp on Linux, and vLLM on a GPU — then wires it into a sandboxed coding agent.

item.title: LocalAI 5.0 hands-on: your own ChatGPT-style server with projects, files, and a Python sandbox
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: LocalAI 5.0 turns the self-hosted inference server into a workspace: server-side chats, Projects, a Files page, and a Python sandbox. This tutorial installs v5.0.0, runs a small model on a CPU-only machine, and proves the chat loop end to end — including the two things that did not work.

item.title: Thinking Machines releases Inkling 2 Mini: a 26B looped model that runs on your laptop
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Thinking Machines Lab’s Inkling 2 Mini reuses its middle layers three times per token to punch above its weight: 26.4B parameters, a 20GB footprint, and agentic coding scores that lead every open-weights model under 100B — and it runs on a MacBook, offline, in airplane mode.

item.title: Google will keep your Gemini chats for two months — even with History off
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Google is stretching Gemini’s retention for temporary chats and history-off conversations from 72 hours to around two months — while splitting history and AI training into separate controls, so you can keep one without the other.

item.title: Hermes Agent hands-on: install the self-improving agent that remembers you and runs your schedule
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Nous Research's Hermes Agent has 265,000 stars and one idea its rivals don't: an agent that writes its own skills, keeps its own notes, and runs your schedule while you sleep. This tutorial installs v0.23.3, wires up a model, and proves the no-agent cron loop end to end.

item.title: RUMOR: Hours after Claude's Riemann claim, a Stanford postdoc posts an all-human proof — rushed out by the AMS president
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Stanford postdoc Alessandro Masullo has posted a proposed proof of the Generalized Riemann Hypothesis — twelve years of work, checked for months by Brian Conrad, and rushed out by AMS president Ravi Vakil hours after Anthropic's AI-assisted claim. It is unpolished, unverified, and explicitly all human.

item.title: Google books Blue Origin to launch its AI servers into orbit in 2029
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Google has booked Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket to carry its first heavy-lift load of solar-powered, TPU-carrying Project Suncatcher satellites into orbit in early 2029 — the boldest test yet of whether AI data centers belong in space.

item.title: Build a coding agent with MiniMax M3.1-Flash: 1M context, five effort levels, and a $0.15-per-million-token bill
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: MiniMax’s M3.1 Flash went GA on October 19 with open weights, a million-token window, and always-on reasoning tuned by five effort levels. This tutorial builds a working coding agent on it — first call, tool loop, vision input, and the self-host recipe — with every client call verified against a local mock of the documented API.

item.title: RUMOR: Alpöge and Buckmaster claim an unforced Navier–Stokes blow-up — paper and Lean code posted, certificate still to come
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: Tristan Buckmaster and Levent Alpöge say they have proved finite-time blow-up for the unforced Navier–Stokes equations — the $1 million Millennium Prize question. A 79-page paper and Lean code are posted, but the certificate the proof relies on has not been released, and no independent expert has verified the claim yet.

item.title: Track anything on live video with tamserve: hands-on with the SAM 2 serving engine
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: tamserve puts Meta's SAM 2 and EdgeTAM behind one serving engine: one model copy tracks every object on every camera. This tutorial installs it, tracks a moving ball through a 6-second clip on CPU, and reports the measured accuracy — 0.1-pixel mean centroid error.

item.title: RUMOR: Anthropic mathematician claims Claude proved the Riemann Hypothesis — Lean code posted, verification pending
item.dc:creator: Priya Nair
item.description: Levent Alpöge, a mathematician at Anthropic, says he and Claude have discovered a proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, formalized in Lean and posted online. No independent expert has verified the claim yet — and the problem's 167-year history says to wait for one.

item.title: AI-powered hacking tool knocks the European Commission's payroll and medical systems offline
item.dc:creator: Marcus Doyle
item.description: The European Commission confirmed an AI-assisted cyberattack that took its payroll and medical reimbursement systems offline for more than ten days. Investigators link the intrusion to ARTEX, an AI penetration-testing framework the FBI flagged a week earlier.

item.title: Run an Instagram account with Claude Code: hands-on with instagram-agent-skill
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: Thirteen Claude skills that run an Instagram account — scored hooks, timed scripts, linted captions, and a humanizer that strips the AI fingerprint. This tutorial runs all five of its Python tools and reports the real numbers, including the ones that stay flagged.

item.title: Speed up your local LLM server: hands-on with inference-optimisation-skill
item.dc:creator: Sofia Almeida
item.description: inference-optimisation turns local LLM tuning into a measurement discipline: ceiling first, one change at a time, controls on both sides. This tutorial runs the loop on a 1.7B model and rejects both levers it tries — four threads collapse decode by 75%, a bigger batch does nothing — proving the baseline was already at 65-90% of its ceiling.
